blog_summary: Adrian Colyer summarizes the Flower Pollination Algorithm (FPA) by Xin-She Yang (2013), a nature-inspired metaheuristic for solving complex constrained optimization problems. The algorithm draws inspiration from the pollination process in plants, modeling both global (cross-pollination via long-distance pollinators) and local (self/abiotic pollination) search strategies. The key insight is the interplay between exploration (via Lévy flight-based global pollination) and exploitation (via flower constancy in local pollination), which enables efficient convergence. Colyer highlights that FPA outperforms traditional genetic algorithms and particle swarm optimization (PSO) in simulations, with exponential convergence rates. The algorithm's simplicity and biological plausibility are noted as strengths.
paper_title: Flower Pollination Algorithm for Global Optimization
paper_abstract: Flower pollination is an intriguing process in the natural world. Its evolutionary characteristics can be used to design new optimization algorithms. In this paper, we propose a new algorithm, namely, flower pollination algorithm, inspired by the pollination process of flowers. We first use ten test functions to validate the new algorithm, and compare its performance with genetic algorithms and particle swarm optimization. Our simulation results show the flower algorithm is more efficient than both GA and PSO. We also use the flower algorithm to solve a nonlinear design benchmark, which shows the convergence rate is almost exponential. Citation Details: Xin-She Yang, Flower pollination algorithm for global optimization, in: Unconventional Computation and Natural Computation 2012, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, Vol. 7445, pp. 240-249 (2012).
